evaluations.evidence: create a new game
evaluations.rationale: Creating a game is a root capability and does not inherently require another backlog story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: Inviting people via a game URL requires a game and its URL to exist first (creation of game).

evaluations.evidence: start a round
evaluations.rationale: Starting a round (entering an item for estimation) inherently requires a game/session to exist.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Viewing the session's items requires those items (and a game/session) to be present, which depends on item-creation stories and game creation.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Selecting an item presupposes the existence of items (added or created in rounds) and a game/session context.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Adding an item is scoped to a game's list and therefore requires a game/session to exist first.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Editing an item requires that an item (and its list in a game/session) already exists.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an item presupposes the existence of the item/list within a game/session.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: Showing estimates relies on the estimation mechanism and participants having joined and submitted estimates.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Accepting an average requires that estimates have been collected from participants (join/estimation features).

evaluations.evidence: have the "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Auto-filling estimate depends on detecting estimators' played cards and the mechanism to reveal/show estimates.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Entering an agreed estimate is meaningful only after estimates have been collected/shown (participant and game features).

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Re-estimating an earlier story requires that prior rounds and their stored items/estimates exist.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Importing stories needs a destination game/session where imported items are stored (game creation).

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Copy/paste of stories must target a game's item list, so it depends on a game/session existing.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Browsing previous games requires games to have been created and persisted (game creation).

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Viewing a game's transcript depends on games/transcripts existing (game creation and storage).

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting a transcript presupposes that transcripts are available (view/export depends on transcript generation/storage).

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: CSV export requires transcripts/games to exist and be stored for export.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game
evaluations.rationale: Deleting a game presumes games are present to be deleted (game creation).

evaluations.evidence: create an account for the application
evaluations.rationale: Account creation is a standalone feature and does not inherently require another backlog story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Logging in requires accounts to exist (account creation).

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Changing account details requires an existing account and typically an authentication mechanism (account creation and login).

evaluations.evidence: delete my account
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an account presupposes that an account exists and the ability to authenticate.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Displaying dates/times in local timezone is a standalone display/formatting feature and does not inherently require another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Password reminders require user accounts with emails stored (account creation).

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Selecting the card sequence is a configuration/setting feature that can be implemented independently.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: Inviting estimators builds on the invitation mechanism (invite by URL), so it depends on the invite feature.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Joining via URL assumes the invite/URL mechanism and that a game exists to join.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Seeing the current item presupposes rounds/items are being selected/created (start round/select item).

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Listing session items requires those items to have been added or created for the game/session.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: Indicating someone has given an estimate requires participants to join and an estimate-submission mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: The reveal-at-once behavior depends on the estimation submission and participant tracking mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
evaluations.rationale: Changing estimates until reveal requires the concept of the draw/reveal and detection of when all have played, which depends on estimation/reveal mechanics.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Viewing prior estimates requires storage/retrieval of previous estimates (history/scrollback features and participants).

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Showing who gave what relies on participant identity and estimate submission being implemented.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: A shared countdown presupposes a multi-participant session and participant presence (join feature).

evaluations.evidence: two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Automatic reset triggered by all participants playing requires detection of all-played state (reveal/estimation mechanics).

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Scrolling back requires that prior rounds and their data have been created and persisted (start rounds / game storage).

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Card-order consistency is a UI/behavior requirement and does not inherently require another story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Allowing changes until draw completion depends on the draw/reveal detection mechanism (estimation/reveal stories).

evaluations.evidence: small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Displaying thumbnail photos depends on user/profile photos being stored/available (account/profile feature).

evaluations.evidence: site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Standards compliance is a cross-cutting developer requirement and does not inherently depend on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: Providing definitions is a standalone documentation requirement and does not require another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: have created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Creating indexes is a developer task that can be implemented independently of other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: have the application function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Cross-browser support is a developer-level requirement and does not inherently depend on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: site comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines
evaluations.rationale: Accessibility compliance is a standalone quality goal and does not require another backlog story first.

evaluations.evidence: have the application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: Performance/responsiveness is a non-dependent quality attribute that can be addressed independently.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Unicode support is a standalone implementation concern and does not inherently depend on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: URL design is an independent UX requirement and does not inherently require another story.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Error pages are a standalone UX requirement and do not inherently depend on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: Privacy/anonymization requirement is a standalone data-storage constraint and does not inherently depend on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: be able to see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: Providing usage metrics requires games and usage data to exist (game creation and gameplay data collection).
